# spawnpoint

> The easiest way to bring your software online. An agent builds a small app, calls
> spawnpoint's MCP server to deploy it, and gets back a public HTTPS link. The only
> manual step is signing in once in a browser.

spawnpoint serves three things: a landing page for people, a **console** where a human
signs in (magic link) and watches their projects, and an **MCP server** that an agent
connects to. Deployed apps run on isolated cloud VMs, each with its own public URL.

spawnpoint is a hosted service. Its hosted MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP) arrives with
the private beta; until then the installer registers a locally running instance (default
`http://localhost:8080/mcp`), which developers can also use any time. This site is the
docs and the installer, not the API: there is no MCP endpoint at spawnpoint.lol.

## Install (Claude Code)

One command does everything scriptable: adds the plugin marketplace, installs the plugin
(two skills), and registers the MCP server:

```
curl -fsSL https://spawnpoint.lol/install | bash
```

The MCP registration points at the hosted origin once your beta access includes one;
override with `SPAWNPOINT_URL=https://... bash`. Until then it defaults to a local dev
instance at `http://localhost:8080`. Or do it by hand:

```
claude plugin marketplace add spawnpoint-inc/spawnpoint-plugin
claude plugin install spawnpoint@spawnpoint
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user spawnpoint http://localhost:8080/mcp
```

Then restart Claude Code, run `/mcp` → spawnpoint → **Authenticate**, and approve in the
browser. Authentication is OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, dynamic client registration) discovered from
the endpoint; the client stores and refreshes the credentials itself. **No key is copied
by hand.** After that, saying **"deploy"** ships the app and returns the link; the
`deploy-to-spawnpoint` skill drives the tool calls.

Any other OAuth-capable MCP client needs only the endpoint URL. Scripts and clients that
cannot do OAuth may send a long-lived `spk_live_…` token (created in the console) as a
bearer credential instead; the endpoint accepts both.

## MCP tools

- `deploy_project`: deploy files as a running app. Takes a name, a runtime
  (`static` | `node` | `python`), an optional entrypoint, the file contents, and optional
  env vars. Returns immediately with the project and its public URL while provisioning
  finishes in the background, so the status starts as `spawning`.
- `list_projects`: list the caller's projects with status and links.
- `terminate_project`: destroy a project's VM and free its URL. Billing stops at once.

## Project status values

`spawning` (VM booting, app being pushed) → `running` (live, URL serves the app), or
`error` if provisioning failed. `terminated` means the VM is destroyed and the URL is
gone. A deploy takes a couple of minutes; the console polls until it settles.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://spawnpoint.lol/getting-started.html): Go from prompt to public link: install the plugin, sign in through the browser, and tell your agent to deploy.
- [MCP server](https://spawnpoint.lol/mcp.html): The Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint and its three tools.
- [API tokens](https://spawnpoint.lol/api-tokens.html): Optional long-lived `spk_live_…` credentials, for scripts and clients that can't sign in through a browser.
- [Plugin repo](https://github.com/spawnpoint-inc/spawnpoint-plugin): the published Claude Code plugin and marketplace manifest.

## About

- [About](https://spawnpoint.lol/about.html): Who's behind spawnpoint: built by Mannan Shukla and Jack Aregood to make shipping small software as easy as sharing a doc.
- [Security](https://spawnpoint.lol/security.html): How spawnpoint protects your account, your credentials, and the code you deploy.
- [Terms of Service](https://spawnpoint.lol/terms.html): The agreement covering accounts, agent-initiated deploys, your content, billing by the hour, and liability.

## Notes

- Every project gets a real HTTPS URL that anyone with the link can open; sharing is by
  link, and the console's share list is for the owner's reference only.
- Terminating is immediate and irreversible: the VM is destroyed and the URL stops
  resolving.
- spawnpoint is aimed at small software (a static site, a Node service, a Python tool),
  not at large multi-service systems.
